report.summary: Chunk 3 of ledger.py: defines intents/intent_events schema, SpineLedger class with __init__ and helpers, including read-only mode and migration support.
risks: intent_events table detail column is TEXT NOT NULL but no default; insert must provide detail.
read-only mode comment mentions -wal/-shm sidecars; not fully filesystem-write-free.
_add_missing_columns runs before _SCHEMA; ordering dependency on trace_id column.
idx_intents_trace is partial (WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL); queries for NULL trace_id will not use it.
PRAGMA query_only=ON set only in read-only mode; not set in read-write mode.
intents.effect_key is nullable; queries may need to handle NULL.
intents.created_ts is TEXT; no format constraint enforced.
busy_timeout is applied per-connection; not persistent.
foreign_keys pragma set but not enforced in read-only mode.
todos: Consider adding NOT NULL constraint or default for intent_events.detail.
Verify that read-only mode's -wal/-shm sidecar creation is acceptable for all callers.
Ensure _add_missing_columns is called before _SCHEMA in all code paths.
Test that read-only mode truly prevents any writes (including sidecars).
Document that idx_intents_trace does not cover NULL trace_id.
Consider adding a CHECK constraint on created_ts format.
Consider setting query_only in read-write mode as well? Not needed per code.

handoff.purpose: Define intents/intent_events table schemas, SpineLedger class with constructor and migration helpers.

symbols.name: intents
symbols.note: SQL table defined via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; columns: id, kind, effect_key, payload, payload_sha, created_ts, trace_id.

symbols.name: intent_events
symbols.note: SQL table defined via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; columns: id, intent_id, state, ts, detail.

symbols.name: idx_intent_events_terminal
symbols.note: Partial index on intent_events(intent_id) WHERE state IN ('COMPLETED','FAILED').

symbols.name: idx_intents_trace
symbols.note: Partial index on intents(trace_id) WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL.

symbols.name: SpineLedger
symbols.note: Crash-safe intent ledger over one SQLite file. Supports read-only mode.

symbols.name: SpineLedger.__init__
symbols.note: Constructor; creates parent directory and runs pragmas/migrations in read-write mode. In read-only mode opens with mode=ro and sets query_only.

symbols.name: SpineLedger._add_missing_columns
symbols.note: Static method; adds missing columns to intents table based on PRAGMA table_info. No-op on fresh database.

claims.text: trace_id is NULLABLE and always will be. An intent recorded outside a traced scope is not an error and must not become one; NULL is the honest record of 'no run was in scope', and a NOT NULL column would have forced a sentinel that reads like a real trace in a join.
claims.why: The schema defines trace_id TEXT (no NOT NULL), so it is nullable. The reasoning is not enforced by SQL but the schema matches the claim.

claims.text: open_intents scans for the ABSENCE of a terminal event; index the states that can end a life so that probe stays a lookup.
claims.why: The function open_intents is not defined in this chunk, so its scanning behavior cannot be verified. The index definition matches the described purpose.

claims.text: The join this whole feature exists to make possible. Partial, because every untraced row shares the value NULL and indexing them would be a scan wearing an index's name.
claims.why: The index is partial with WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL, matching the rationale that NULL values are not indexed.

claims.text: One connection per instance. check_same_thread=False plus an internal lock lets a single instance be shared across threads (the loop's worker and a status reader) without two statements interleaving on one connection; separate instances on the same file are arbitrated by SQLite itself under busy_timeout.
claims.why: The constructor sets check_same_thread=False and uses an RLock (_lock). The docstring's description matches the implementation.

claims.text: A READER MUST NOT WRITE. The normal path creates the parent directory, sets journal_mode=WAL (which writes the file header) and runs migrations inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE -- so merely OPENING a ledger to look at it mutates it. That is intolerable for callers whose whole contract is that they change nothing (the picker's --dry-run ranks a queue and must stay a read). SQLite enforces it here rather than this class promising it: mode=ro fails any write at the engine, so a future edit that adds one cannot pass tests.
claims.why: The read-only branch uses uri with mode=ro and does not call _apply_pragmas or _migrate. SQLite will reject writes. The claim about the normal path mutating is consistent with the read-write branch creating parent dir and calling _apply_pragmas (which sets WAL).

claims.text: HONEST LIMIT: opening a WAL database read-only still creates the -wal/-shm sidecars, because the shared-memory index is how WAL reads work. The ledger's CONTENTS are untouched (a test pins the file's sha256 across a read), but this is not 'touches nothing on disk', and a genuinely read-only filesystem will fail the open -- which callers surface as an error rather than as a silently empty history.
claims.why: The comment is accurate about SQLite behavior; it is a limitation acknowledged in the code.

claims.text: Runs BEFORE the _SCHEMA statements, and the ordering is load-bearing: idx_intents_trace names trace_id, so on a v1 database the index creation fails outright unless the column exists first.
claims.why: The order of execution relative to _SCHEMA is not visible in this chunk; it depends on the caller. The claim is logical but unverifiable here.

claims.text: Driven off PRAGMA table_info rather than off the recorded schema_version, because the two can disagree -- a database created by a newer checkout and then opened by an older one has the column without the version, and a version number is a claim about the file while table_info is the file. Ask the file.
claims.why: The implementation uses PRAGMA table_info(intents) to discover columns, as described.

claims.text: On a FRESH database table_info returns nothing (no table yet), so this is a no-op and CREATE TABLE installs the full v2 shape.
claims.why: The code iterates over results of PRAGMA table_info; if no table exists, it returns empty, so the loop does nothing.

observations.what: intent_events.detail column is TEXT NOT NULL but no default value; insert must provide detail.
Read-only mode comment acknowledges -wal/-shm sidecar creation; not fully filesystem-write-free.
_add_missing_columns is staticmethod and expects to be called before _SCHEMA; ordering dependency not enforced by this class.
idx_intents_trace is partial (WHERE trace_id IS NOT NULL); queries filtering on trace_id IS NULL will not use this index.
PRAGMA query_only=ON is set only in read-only mode; read-write mode does not set it, but writes are expected.
intents.effect_key is nullable; queries may need to handle NULL.
intents.created_ts is TEXT; no format constraint (e.g., ISO8601) enforced by schema.
busy_timeout is applied per-connection via PRAGMA; not persistent in the database file.
foreign_keys pragma is set in _apply_pragmas but not in read-only mode; read-only mode does not set it.
